description: OSPF Protocol Conformance Analyzer — combines tshark pcap analysis, RFC 2328 FSM validation, and scapy test packet generation

OSPFAnalyzer.description: Main analyzer class. Requires tshark on PATH and scapy importable.

constructor_params.topology_file: str - path to topology JSON file

extract_packets.description: Extract OSPF packets from a pcap file using tshark (invoked as a subprocess). Must handle Hello packets at minimum.
extract_packets.returns: list[dict] - each dict has keys: timestamp (float), src_ip (str), src_router (str - OSPF Router ID), type (str - 'Hello'), hello_interval (int), dead_interval (int), priority (int), dr (str - Designated Router IP), bdr (str - Backup DR IP), neighbors (list[str] - active neighbor Router IDs)

analyze_capture.description: Analyze a pcap from one router's perspective. Infer FSM events from packet observations: HelloReceived from any neighbor Hello; 2-WayReceived when perspective router is in the neighbor's Hello neighbor list AND current state is Init; 1-Way when perspective router is NOT in the list AND current state >= 2-Way; InactivityTimer when gap between consecutive Hellos from a neighbor exceeds that neighbor's RouterDeadInterval. Apply adjacency decisions using DR/BDR from Hello packets and network type from topology.

params.router_id: str - perspective router's OSPF Router ID

returns.transitions: list[dict] - each: {timestamp (float), neighbor (str), event (str), from_state (str), to_state (str)}

process_trace.description: Process a JSON event trace through the FSM engine. Creates fresh FSMs per trace. Deep-copies network topology for DR/BDR updates within a trace. If an event has a 'dr_update' field, update network DR/BDR and FSM role properties BEFORE processing.

params.trace_file: str - path to trace JSON (has 'trace_id' and 'events' array)

returns.transitions: list[dict] - each: {time (int), router (str), neighbor (str), event (str), from_state (str), to_state (str)}

validate_transitions.description: Validate claimed state transitions in a trace file against the RFC spec. For each transition, create a temp FSM in the claimed from_state with current network context, process the event, check if expected to_state matches claimed to_state. DR/BDR updates accumulate.

params.trace_file: str - path to trace JSON with 'transitions' array having from_state/to_state fields

generate_test_pcap.description: Generate an OSPF Hello pcap file using scapy. Must use scapy.contrib.ospf classes.

params.packets_spec: list[dict] - each: {router_id (str), src_ip (str), dst_ip (str, default '224.0.0.5'), hello_interval (int, default 10), dead_interval (int, default 40), priority (int, default 1), dr (str, default '0.0.0.0'), bdr (str, default '0.0.0.0'), neighbors (list[str], default []), timestamp (float, default 0)}

generate_test_pcap.returns: str - path to generated pcap file

violation_types.dead_interval_exceeded: No Hello received from neighbor within RouterDeadInterval of last Hello
violation_types.hello_interval_mismatch: HelloInterval or DeadInterval values differ between routers sharing a network
violation_types.invalid_transition: Claimed FSM transition does not match RFC 2328 Section 10.3

trace_event_format.event: str - FSM event name from Section 10.2

dr_update._note: Optional. Update network DR/BDR before processing.
